Current-engine five-pair trials: Lua whole-frame -0.74% normal (95% mean ratio .98933-.99812), stress -0.084% inconclusive; Rust +0.54% normal and +0.022% stress both inconclusive. This is a parity/work-reduction selection; no Rust or general whole-frame speedup is claimed.

optimization.title: Flove matched target selection
optimization.change: Both use cumulative weights in the original f32 addition order and select the first prefix strictly greater than the same random sample. Lua caches immutable definitions and order-frame reads, reuses the selected snapshot position and removes an unused position query; Rust matches lazy snapshot creation and Lua private order-frame publication. UI is unchanged. Existing source-pair method; current NVIDIA engine and unchanged guards. Both phases use the same retained 0f SDK normal modules so this isolates the CDF/cache change; final selected modules are rebuilt against SDK782. The original integration/image and before/after world proofs use the geometry-fixed prototype and remain recorded with that binary identity.
